Zheng He: Chinese Admiral and diplomat (1371–1433/1435)

Who among these is an astronomer?
Mikhail Lomonosov is an astronomer. One of the founders of modern geology, Lomonosov was also a poet and influenced the formation of the modern Russian literary language.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Gerardus Mercator is a mathematician. Gerardus Mercator (5 March 1512 – 2 December 1594) was a Flemish geographer, cosmographer and cartographer.
What is the atomic number of Zirconium?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
What is the atomic number of Francium?
Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.
In what year was Ursula von der Leyen born?
Ursula von der Leyen: Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.

Ondansetron: Pfizer. It is also effective for treating gastroenteritis.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
These tropical arachnids are nicknamed 'whip-spiders,' yet they spin no silk and carry no venom — their name actually means 'blunt tail.' Which order are they?
Amblypygi is an order of arachnids also known as whip-spiders or tailless whip-scorpions, not to be confused with whip-scorpions or vinegaroons that belong to the related order Uropygi.
A physician who called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress, this Russian writer produced four stage classics and ranks among modernism's founders — who is he?
Anton Chekhov was Russian dramatist and author (1860–1904).
This British mathematician coined the term 'mathematical induction' and is best remembered for a pair of laws linking conjunction, disjunction, and negation in logic — who was he?
Augustus De Morgan (27 June 1806 - 18 March 1871) was a British mathematician and logician.

Known only from larval and juvenile specimens until video footage of much larger adults surfaced, this deep-sea cephalopod genus holds its long, elbow-like arms perpendicular to its body — what is it?
Bigfin squid are a group of rarely seen cephalopods with a distinctive morphology.
Despite being fully Turing-complete, this minimalist 1993 esoteric language allows only eight commands and takes its unusual name from a slang term for utter confusion — what language is it?
Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Mller.
This biological family includes domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, foxes, and jackals, found on every continent except Antarctica. What family is it?
Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like plant is a staple in calming herbal tea, beer brewing, and even garden ground cover — what is it?
Chamomile (American English) or camomile (British English; see spelling differences) (or) is the common name for several daisy-like plants of the family Asteraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Specialists in this branch of medicine handle skin infections, cancers, hair loss, and cosmetic concerns, sometimes even life-threatening conditions like severe burns — which medical field?
Dermatology is the branch of medicine dealing with the skin.
A German-born British economist, he championed human-scale, appropriate technology in a hugely influential 1973 book ranked among the 100 most important since WWII — who is he?

E. F. Schumacher (16 August 1911 - 4 September 1977) was a German-born British statistician and economist who is best known for his proposals for human-scale, decentralised and appropriate technologies.

This genus's tapering spacing of stem nodes toward the tip is credited with inspiring John Napier's work on logarithms; today it's the sole living genus of an ancient, spore-producing plant lineage nicknamed horsetail — which genus?
Equisetum (horsetail) is the only living genus in Equisetaceae, a family of vascular plants that reproduce by spores rather than seeds.

Patented in 1979 but not used medically until 1996, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergic rhinitis and hives while causing far less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what's the drug?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.

A bulbous Allium native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, this kitchen staple counts the chive, leek, and shallot among its cousins and was prized by ancient Babylonians and Egyptians — what is it?
Garlic (Allium sativum) is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.

In this heart condition, muscle tissue — most often in the wall between the ventricles — thickens for no obvious reason, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes its electrical rhythm — name the condition?
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.

This Russian and Soviet physiologist discovered classical conditioning through famous experiments involving dogs, and won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his separate research into digestion — who is he?
Born in Los Angeles to South Korean immigrant parents, this NASA astronaut and physician previously served as a Navy SEAL on over 100 combat missions — who is he?
Jonny Kim (born 5 February 1984) is an American NASA astronaut, physician, U.S.

Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine and beloved in Singapore and Malaysia, this spicy noodle dish swims in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind, topped with prawns or chicken — what's its name?
Laksa is a spicy noodle dish popular in Southeast Asia.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Nicknamed "quicksilver," this is the only metallic element that stays liquid at room temperature, and it's often mined as the red mineral cinnabar — which element is it?
Mercury (element) is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.

Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this colorless noble gas is famous for the distinctive bright-red glow it emits, which led to its immediate identification as a new element — what gas, symbol Ne, is it?
Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.
This Persian polymath and poet was the first to provide a general geometric solution to all third-degree polynomial equations, using the intersection of conic sections. Who is he?
Omar Khayyam (1048-1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
Designed by Niklaus Wirth to encourage structured programming and named after a French mathematician-philosopher, this language was developed in the pattern of ALGOL 60 — name it?

Pascal (programming language) is an imperative and procedural programming language, designed by Niklaus Wirth as a small, efficient language intended to encourage good programming practices using structured programming and data structuring.
Its name comes from the Greek for 'love of wisdom,' and physics and psychology were once branches of it — what is this rational inquiry into existence and knowledge?

Philosophy (from Ancient Greek philosophia, lit. 'love of wisdom') is a systematic study of general and fundamental questions concerning topics like existence, knowledge, mind, reason, language, and value.
Abundant throughout the plant kingdom, this broad class of naturally occurring phenolic compounds includes flavonoids and ellagitannin — what is the family called?
Polyphenol are a large family of naturally occurring phenols.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.

Native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries have long been used for cordial and wine, and it also appears in traditional medicine and dietary supplements — name this plant?
Sambucus nigra is a temperate species of tree or shrub in the family Viburnaceae native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East.
Before becoming the first woman on Facebook's board, this executive ran global sales at Google and assisted Lawrence Summers at the World Bank — who later wrote 'Lean In'?
Sheryl Sandberg (born August 28, 1969) is an American technology executive, philanthropist and writer.

Extending from the base of the brainstem down to the lower back, this tubular bundle of nervous tissue is covered by the meninges and, together with the brain, makes up the central nervous system — name this structure?

Spinal cord is a long, thin, tubular structure made up of nervous tissue that extends from the medulla oblongata in the lower brainstem to the lumbar region of the vertebral column (backbone) of vertebrate animals.
Time named this marine biologist its first "Hero for the Planet" in 1998, the same year she became a National Geographic Explorer — and she was also NOAA's first chief scientist. Who is she?
Sylvia Earle (born August 30, 1935) is an American marine biologist, oceanographer, explorer, writer, and lecturer.
Writing in 1798, this English cleric-economist warned that abundance only fuels population growth, eventually restoring poverty and hardship for the lower classes — who is he?
Thomas Robert Malthus (13/14 February 1766 - 29 December 1834) was an English economist, cleric, and scholar influential in the fields of political economy and demography.
Egypt and Iraq both flew this Soviet-designed jet bomber in wars against Israel, and China still produces an updated license-built version, the H-6K — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-16 (USAF/DOD reporting name Type 39; NATO reporting name: Badger) is a twin-engined jet strategic heavy bomber used by the Soviet Union.

Many of these carrion-eating birds sport a bald head that stays clean while feeding and helps with temperature control — and they'll even urinate on their own legs to cool off. What kind of bird is it?
Vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
Also called humped cattle for the fatty growth on its shoulders, this South Asian breed group is used for everything from plowing to dairy, and even kept as pets in miniature form — what is it?
Zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.

Typically affecting women between 35 and 50, this uterine condition occurs when endometrial-like tissue grows within the muscular wall of the uterus, causing painful, heavy periods — what is it called?
Adenomyosis: Extension of endometrial tissue into the myometrium.
On 18 March 1965, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first person to walk in space, spending over twelve minutes outside his capsule during a Voskhod mission — who is he?

Capable of constantly changing its shape by extending and retracting temporary 'false feet,' this single-celled organism turns up across nearly every branch of the eukaryotic tree of life — what is it?

Their larvae — nicknamed "doodlebugs" in North America for the marks they leave — dig sandy pits to trap passing ants, while the dusk-flying adults are often mistaken for dragonflies. What insect is this?
This American psychiatrist and pharmaceutical marketer amassed the world's largest personal collection of Chinese art, later donated to the Smithsonian — who is he?
Arthur M. Sackler: American physician and executive (1913–1987)
Sold under the brand name Lioresal, this muscle relaxant treats spasticity from spinal cord injuries or MS and is sometimes used off-label for alcohol withdrawal — what is it?
Baclofen: Gabapentinoid and Skeletal Muscle Relaxant.
This flowering plant's cultivated varieties include a sugar-producing root crop, the crimson garden vegetable known as beetroot, and the leafy green called chard — what species is it?
Beta vulgaris: Species of flowering plant. Beta vulgaris (beet) is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Betoideae of the family Amaranthaceae.
A twinjet successor to a trijet predecessor, this American narrow-body airliner entered commercial service with Eastern Air Lines on New Year's Day 1983. Which aircraft?
Its name means 'thunder lizard,' and though long dismissed as just another sauropod genus, a 2015 study restored this dinosaur's status as distinct — which one?
Brontosaurus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994.
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Nicknamed the jade plant or money plant, this low-maintenance South African succulent thrives on neglect and barely any water — what's its botanical name?
Crassula ovata: Species of succulent. It is sometimes referred to as the money tree; however, Pachira aquatica also has this nickname.
Designed to replace an earlier delta-wing jet for the French Air Force, this fourth-generation single-engine fighter first flew in March 1978 — which aircraft?
Dassault Mirage 2000: French jet fighter aircraft. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
In this heart condition, the heart chambers become enlarged and lose their ability to pump blood effectively, with causes ranging from genetics to alcohol and cocaine use — what is it called?
Dilated cardiomyopathy: Condition involving an enlarged, ineffective heart.

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

In this lung disease the walls between the alveoli break down, merging tiny air sacs into enlarged spaces that shrink the surface available for gas exchange and starve the blood of oxygen. Which condition is it?
Emphysema: Chronic lung condition. Emphysema is a condition of the lung marked by abnormal enlargement of the alveoli with loss of pulmonary elasticity.
This Hungarian-American theoretical physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus and elementary particles — who was he?
Eugene Wigner: Hungarian-American physicist and mathematician (1902–1995)
This Stanford computer scientist built ImageNet, the vast labeled dataset that ignited the deep-learning revolution in computer vision in the 2010s. Who is she?

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
Native to North America, this genus of roughly 50 flowering plant species is better known by its common name — the sunflowers — and includes food crops for humans and livestock alike — which genus?

Helianthus: Genus of flowering plants, the sunflowers. Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
Caused by a buildup of bilirubin, this condition turns the skin and eyes yellowish and affects an estimated 80% of newborns in their first week of life — what is it?
Jaundice: Abnormal yellowish skin colour caused by high level of bilirubin.
This genus of coniferous trees and shrubs in the cypress family includes a species that forms the world's highest-known forest, at 4,900 metres in the Himalayas — what is it called?

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'hump,' this abnormal, excessive curving of the upper spine can result from osteoporosis, disc disease, or a condition common in teens called Scheuermann's disease — what is it called?
Kyphosis: Excessive convex curvature of the lower and middle spine.
Often called the last physicist to master every branch of the field, this Soviet scientist co-discovered the density matrix method and developed the theory of superfluidity — who is he?
Also called dragon's eye, this tropical fruit tree from the soapberry family produces fruit similar to lychee but with a milder aroma, and is native to Southeast Asia and southern China — what is it?
Longan: Species of tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes and caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, which disease's symptoms typically begin 10 to 15 days after infection?
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
With velvety fur, tiny eyes, and powerful digging forelimbs, this subterranean mammal aerates garden soil and feasts on earthworms and slugs despite being seen as a pest — what is it?
Mole (animal): Common name for several small mammals.
This condition describes an abnormally dilated pupil that remains enlarged even in bright light, often triggered by trauma, disease, or certain drugs — what is it called?
Mydriasis: Excessive dilation of the pupil.
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
This Stanford biologist became famous — and controversial — for his 1968 book warning that runaway population growth would bring famine and resource depletion. Who was he?
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
Caused by a single mutation in the LMNA gene, this rare disorder causes children to age dramatically faster than normal, with most not living past their twenties — which condition?
Progeria: Genetic disorder that causes early aging.
In Euclidean geometry, which fundamental relation says the square on a right triangle's longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two — famously written a² + b² = c²?
Pythagorean theorem: Relation between sides of a right triangle.
This biological process comes in two forms — asexual, as seen in cloning, and sexual, which combines gametes carrying half the usual chromosome count — what's the process called?
Reproduction: Biological process. Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms – offspring – are produced from their parent or parents.
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine — and the first American-born one — this physicist shared the 1977 award for developing the radioimmunoassay. Who was she?
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow: American medical physicist (1921–2011)
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle and fat, this rare cancer is only about 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones — what is it?
Sarcoma: Cancer originating in connective tissue.
A slender African cat with a tiny head and enormous ears, this golden, black-spotted hunter is the sole member of its genus and stands tall on remarkably long legs — which wild cat is it?
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?
Sweet potato: Species of edible plant.
More than 30,000 unsaturated hydrocarbons built on (C5H8)n units, produced mostly by plants (especially conifers) and used by some insects as defense — what class of natural compounds is this?
Terpene: Class of oily organic compounds found in plants.
Arrested 36 times and branded "the most dangerous man in America" by Nixon, this Harvard psychologist founded a Psilocybin Project and became the face of psychedelic advocacy — who was he?
Estimated to date back to the end of the Jurassic period roughly 156 million years ago, this fungal genus includes several species of truffles prized as culinary delicacies — which genus?
Tuber (fungus): Genus of fungi. Tuber is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Nicknamed the 'vampire fish' for feeding on the blood of larger fish through their gills, this tiny Amazonian catfish is infamous for an alleged, rare habit of entering human body openings — what is it?
Vandellia cirrhosa: Species of ray-finned fish.
Named after the German city where it originated, this all-purpose gun dog breed was officially recognized in 1891 — what breed is it?
Weimaraner: German breed of dog. The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
Following her husband's death, this Russian economist and activist vowed to carry on his opposition work and now chairs the Human Rights Foundation — who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya: Russian economist and political activist (born 1976)

The symbol for oxygen is O. Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.

Manufactured by Piaggio since 1946 and named after the Italian word for 'wasp,' this brand of scooters became an Italian design icon — name the brand?
Vespa (Italian; Italian for 'wasp') is an Italian brand of scooters and mopeds manufactured by Piaggio. The Vespa has evolved from a single model motor scooter manufactured in 1946 by Piaggio & Co.

Founded in 1978 by Mel and Patricia Ziegler as a safari-and-travel clothing company, this Gap-owned retailer was reimagined in the 2020s with campaigns evoking luxury brands like Ralph Lauren — what is it?
Banana Republic: American clothing and accessory retailer.

A banker who once served as CEO of Banco Guayaquil, this politician became Ecuador's 47th president in 2021 after years as a vocal critic of the Correa administration — who is he?
Guillermo Lasso: President of Ecuador from 2021 to 2023.

Founded in Cincinnati in 1883, this American grocery giant also runs fuel centers, pharmacies, and in-store medical clinics, with about two-thirds of its workforce under union contracts — which retailer?
Headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland, this conglomerate has been the world's largest publicly held food company since 2014, with 29 brands each topping a billion in annual sales — what is it?
Nestlé: Swiss multinational food and drink company.
Incorporated in 2011 but tracing its engines back to 1904, this British aerospace giant holds roughly 12% of the commercial jet-engine market — which company?
Rolls-Royce Holdings: British multinational aerospace and defence company.

Founded by Sir Jack Cohen in London in 1919, this British retailer commands more than a quarter of the UK grocery market and ranked as the world's 15th-largest retailer by revenue in 2023 — which company?
Tesco: British multinational retail groceries company.
